about: Source of truth for the traceability matrix (Week 4: every requirement traces to a threat, business need or regulation, to the code that meets it, and to the test that proves it). npm run trace checks every link and rewrites TRACEABILITY.md; a test fails if any link is broken or the file is out of date.

threats.threat: Guessing or reusing a staff password to sign in as that person
Forging, stealing or replaying a session cookie
A member of staff denies a refund, discount or price change
A user gives themself or a friend a higher role
Changing prices, totals or quantities in a request
Changing an ID in a request to read another person's order or bill
A waiter or kitchen user calls cashier, manager or admin routes directly
Another website makes a signed-in member of staff submit a change (CSRF)
A forged or copied gateway callback marks an unpaid bill as paid
A double click or a slow gateway charges a customer twice
One person issues a large refund to themself or an accomplice
Customer names and numbers read from the screens, database or a backup
Flooding the booking form or the API to block customers and staff
Script typed into a name or note runs in another person's browser (XSS)
Editing, deleting or re-hashing audit entries to hide misuse
Uploading a script or HTML file disguised as a photo
A compromised app account rewrites history or reads other databases
Stack traces, secrets or passwords leak through errors or log files
An insider exports data in bulk before leaving
An outside service is slow or down and blocks the till
The server starts with a missing or weak key, or without database credentials
Data lost to disk failure, ransomware or a mistaken delete

requirements.text: The system shall require a TOTP authenticator code for every staff sign-in, with single-use recovery codes.
tests: a correct password alone gives no session (MFA is mandatory)
a code cannot be used twice
a recovery code works exactly once

requirements.text: The system shall store passwords only as Argon2id hashes and refuse passwords under 12 characters, without mixed character types, or built on a common word.
tests: passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes
a common word dressed up with capitals, digits and symbols does not pass
the server refuses one when a person changes their password

requirements.text: The system shall lock an account for 15 minutes after 3 failed passwords or authenticator codes, counted on the server.
tests: 3 failures lock the account, and the right password is then refused
wrong MFA codes also count towards the lock
the right password alone does not reset the count, so authenticator codes cannot be guessed forever
a new browser cannot reset the lock
a locked account cannot pass an authenticator re-check or change its password

requirements.text: Sessions shall be a signed HttpOnly __Host- cookie backed by a server record, ending after 5 idle minutes or 8 hours, and revocable at once.
tests: forged tokens are refused: alg none, wrong key, no server record
5 idle minutes end the session
the 8-hour limit applies however active the session is
sign-out ends the session on the server, so a copied cookie stops working

requirements.text: Every route shall check the caller's role against one permission table, and anything not listed shall be denied.
tests: every role against every route (RBAC matrix)
every route has a guard, so none can be left open by accident (complete mediation)
nobody can change their own role or status

requirements.text: A waiter shall see and change only their own orders, and a cashier only today's bills.
tests: one waiter cannot see or change another waiter's order
a cashier cannot open a past day's bill by its number; a manager can

requirements.text: The server shall calculate every price and total from stored data and refuse requests with unknown fields, wrong types or operator objects.
tests: the total is calculated on the server; the browser cannot set it (Rs 2,500 to 250)
NoSQL operator objects are refused
negative, zero, fractional, huge and non-numeric quantities are refused

requirements.text: Every change shall carry the session's CSRF token and come from the cafe's own origin.
tests: a signed-in change needs the CSRF token
requests from another site, or with no Origin, are blocked

requirements.text: Pages shall run under a strict Content Security Policy with Trusted Types, and the browser code shall never build HTML from strings.
tests: the CSP has no exceptions: no inline styles, no third-party hosts, Trusted Types required
script text in a name is stored as plain text, and shown as plain text
no browser script writes HTML from strings or stores business data on the device (findings 14, 20, 30)
every form posts, so a password or number can never end up in a URL or access log

requirements.text: Refunds over Rs 5,000 and any change affecting an Admin shall need a second person, and sensitive actions a fresh authenticator code.
tests: a large refund waits for a different person with a fresh code
one Admin alone cannot create another Admin; a second Admin must approve
need a fresh authenticator code as well as the Manager role
the target of a request cannot approve it
the Admin who set up a Manager's account cannot approve that Manager's large refund
one Admin can disable a compromised Admin at once, and it raises an alert

requirements.text: Every security-relevant action shall be written to a signed, hash-chained audit log in the same transaction, with the actor taken from the session.
tests: detects a recalculated hash, because the attacker cannot sign it
if the audit entry fails, the action it describes does not happen
the recorded waiter is always the signed-in person
an action that cannot be recorded does not happen (fail-secure audit)
a row added outside the chain fails verification and is never shown
verifying while actions are being written gives no false alarm

requirements.text: Customer names, numbers and notes shall be encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, masked for roles that do not need them, and each full view logged.
tests: name, phone and notes are encrypted at rest
only a Manager or Admin can see the full number, and it is logged
waiters see a masked phone; only a Manager or Admin can reveal it, with a log entry (finding 32)
a shortened GCM authentication tag is refused, so forged values cannot be accepted
searching by number is limited per person and recorded, without storing the number
opening reservations is recorded once an hour per person, without repeating on every refresh
opening one bill is recorded, and many views raise an alert
every database file is encrypted at rest with AES-256, and the key stays out of git and the image

requirements.text: Uploaded photos shall be checked by their file signature, limited to 2 MB, given random names and stored outside the web root.
tests: scripts, SVG, HTML and disguised files are refused and recorded
a file over 2 MB is refused
uploads cannot be stored inside the web root
content hidden after a real image, and its metadata, do not survive
a file with an image header that is not really an image is refused and recorded

requirements.text: Orders, payments and refunds shall run once per idempotency key, in transactions, with version checks against lost updates.
tests: a double click creates one order and takes stock once
double-clicking Pay with one key charges one bill
an edit from an out-of-date screen is refused rather than overwriting

requirements.text: Gateway callbacks shall be HMAC-signed, recent, single-use and checked against the stored amount, and no second payment shall start while a charge is in progress.
tests: forged, old, wrong-amount and malformed callbacks are refused
a copied gateway callback is accepted only once
no second payment is taken while a card charge is still waiting for the gateway
a late approval for a bill already paid another way is recorded and raises an alert
a callback that failed part-way can be retried; only a processed one is a replay

requirements.text: The system shall raise de-duplicated alerts for failed sign-ins per person and per address, denials, bulk exports, number views, refund spikes and payment conflicts, and shall also alert on sign-ins from a new network, access, price and security setting changes, many record views and stopped backups, in a list a flood cannot hide.
tests: failed sign-ins, denials, exports, number views and refunds each raise an alert
one password tried against many usernames from one address raises an alert (password spraying)
a flood updates one alert instead of creating many
a flood of low-value alerts cannot push a serious one out of the Admin's list
the most serious alerts are listed first
a role change raises an alert
many price changes by one person raise an alert
a changed security setting is recorded by name and raises an alert
a new network raises an alert; a known one, and a person's first sign-in, do not
an overdue review raises a reminder, and recording a review clears it
a review must say something, and only an Admin can record one

requirements.text: The app shall use a least-privilege database account that cannot change or delete audit entries, and production shall refuse to start without database credentials.
tests: the app account can add audit entries but cannot change or delete them
production refuses a database connection with no username and password (least privilege)
the app's database account cannot add indexes to the audit log, so it cannot erase it with a TTL index

requirements.text: The server shall refuse to start with missing or weak secrets, and errors shall show a generic message with a reference only.
tests: refuses to start without secrets
refuses weak or wrongly sized keys
broken JSON gives a clean error with no stack trace
sign-in fails closed and reveals nothing
an unsupported charset is a client error, not a server error

requirements.text: Exports shall be limited per person and recorded, and CSV cells shall never run as spreadsheet formulas.
tests: exports are logged, limited per person, and safe to open in a spreadsheet
CSV cells that a spreadsheet would run as formulas are neutralised
the export limit is shared by every export, per person

requirements.text: Under a request flood the system shall keep serving other users: limits per address, per person and for pages, body-size limits and request timeouts.
tests: the general API rate limit applies
each signed-in person has a limit, so one person cannot use up a shared cafe address
pages and health checks are limited too
oversized bodies are refused
one address can send only a limited number of requests
one address can read the public API only a limited number of times
only a few passwords are hashed at once, and an overfull queue is refused
staff sessions and public traffic are served by separate app processes
requirements.note: Measured under a simulated flood in LOAD-TEST.md: no staff request failed, but response times do not meet the Week 4 example of no more than 10% slower.

requirements.text: A slow or failed payment gateway or message provider shall not stop the till: payments fall back to Pending Payment and messages are queued with retries.
tests: a timeout leaves the bill Pending Payment, the till responsive and revenue unchanged
failures retry with growing gaps, then raise one Admin alert
a gateway crash is treated the same as a timeout

requirements.text: Data shall be recoverable from an encrypted, checksummed backup, and the server shall shut down without cutting off requests in progress.
tests: a restore brings back every record, and the audit chain still verifies
an altered file or the wrong key is refused
a request in progress finishes, then the database closes and the process exits cleanly
a backup taken while the cafe is busy restores with a valid audit chain
old backups are removed, and only files this tool made
no recent backup raises an alert, and a recent one does not
the status record stays out of backups, so a restore still starts from an empty database

requirements.text: Security shall not get in the way of a busy shift: staff stay signed in while working, but automatic screen refreshes never keep an idle session open.
tests: background refreshes do not keep an idle session alive

requirements.text: Production shall run over HTTPS as an unprivileged, read-only container from a pinned minimal image, with only the proxy reachable from outside and the database on a private network.
tests: runs on a pinned, minimal base as an unprivileged user
every service is read-only, drops all capabilities and cannot gain privileges
only Caddy is reachable from outside, and the database network has no route out
the app never receives the database administrator password or the backup key
every action is pinned to a commit, and the default token is read-only
allows a second Admin, then refuses, so it cannot get round the second-Admin rule

requirements.text: A customer's personal data shall be erasable on request, keeping only the bill totals needed for tax records (right to erasure).
requirements.source: GDPR Article 17 right to erasure; Pakistan Personal Data Protection Bill
tests: erasing removes the person but keeps the bill totals, and needs a fresh code

requirements.text: Personal data shall be kept no longer than 90 days, collected only as needed, and explained in a privacy notice.
requirements.source: GDPR Article 5 storage limitation and data minimisation
tests: retention removes personal data after 90 days, and keeps recent data
the privacy notice tells customers what the security log keeps
an unknown username is never stored, in case a password was typed there

requirements.text: No card or wallet details shall ever be received or stored, keeping the cafe outside card-data audit scope.
tests: approved card payment is paid, with no card details anywhere

requirements.text: A breach shall be detectable and reportable within 72 hours: tamper checks raise alerts, and logs hold no passwords, tokens or codes.
requirements.source: GDPR Article 33 breach notification within 72 hours
tests: the Admin screen can verify, and a broken chain raises an alert
logs hold no cookies, tokens, passwords or codes
requirements.note: The step-by-step breach runbook is INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md, written in Phase 7.

requirements.text: Refunds, approvals, staff access changes and customer erasure shall be signed with the acting person's own device key (ECDSA P-256), which the server verifies, keeps and can check again, so the person cannot later deny the action.
requirements.source: Week 2, slide 15: non-repudiation through digital signatures
tests: an unsigned staff change is refused and nothing changes
a signed change goes through, and the signature is kept and recorded
a captured signed request cannot be replayed
a signature over a changed body, another person's key, a removed key or an old time is refused
refunds and approvals need a signature too
a key can be added straight after sign-in, but later only after a fresh code
only P-256 public keys are accepted, and private parts or markup are refused
every kept signature verifies, and a changed record is found

requirements.text: Staff shall be able to sign in and confirm sensitive actions with a passkey that needs the device's fingerprint, face or PIN, and that only works on this site.
requirements.source: Week 2, scenario 11: biometric access; phishing (Attackers deck)
tests: password then passkey signs in
a look-alike site, a skipped fingerprint or PIN check, a replay or someone else's passkey is refused
a passkey without the device's fingerprint or PIN check is refused when added
a passkey can confirm a sensitive action, and removing one needs that confirmation

requirements.text: Signing in with a recovery code shall also require the answer to the person's security question, stored only as an Argon2id hash.
requirements.source: Week 2, scenario 2: a security question as well as the password
tests: a recovery code alone is not enough once a question is set
setting a question needs a fresh code, and the answer is kept only as a hash
the question is shown only after the password step

requirements.text: A sign-in from a country not seen before for that account shall raise a high alert, using address data held locally.
requirements.source: Week 2, scenario 7: access from an unusual location
tests: addresses are placed in countries locally, and private addresses in none
the first country is learned quietly, and a sign-in from a new one raises a high alert

requirements.text: Email shall be sent only over TLS 1.2 or later to a verified server, and shall carry no personal details.
requirements.source: Week 2, scenario 6: sensitive email encrypted automatically
tests: a notice is sent only after the connection switches to TLS, and holds no guest details
a server that cannot encrypt receives nothing, and the message stays queued for a retry
a server whose certificate cannot be verified receives nothing

requirements.text: Staff may sign in with an organisation account through OpenID Connect, with PKCE, a browser-bound state, a nonce and a checked ID token signature; the cafe's own second factor is still required.
requirements.source: Week 2, slide 29: use standard protocols such as OAuth or OpenID Connect
tests: a linked organisation account replaces the password, and the cafe's own code is still required
a callback from another browser, a replayed callback, a wrong nonce or a forged token is refused
one organisation account cannot be linked to two people, and unlinking needs a fresh code

requirements.text: Requests shall pass a web application firewall running the OWASP Core Rule Set in blocking mode, and per-address rate limits, before reaching the app.
requirements.source: Week 2, slide 25: firewalls and intrusion detection; defence in depth
tests: Caddy runs the OWASP Core Rule Set in blocking mode and limits requests per address

misuseCases.useCase: A waiter signs in with password and authenticator code.
misuseCases.misuseCase: An attacker with a leaked password tries authenticator codes until one works.
misuseCases.response: Three wrong codes lock the account for 15 minutes, and repeated failures raise an alert.
tests: the right password alone does not reset the count, so authenticator codes cannot be guessed forever

misuseCases.useCase: A waiter edits their own order before the kitchen starts it.
misuseCases.misuseCase: A waiter changes the order ID to edit another waiter's order.
misuseCases.response: The order looks the same as one that does not exist (404).
tests: one waiter cannot see or change another waiter's order

misuseCases.useCase: A cashier takes payment for a served table.
misuseCases.misuseCase: The cashier sends a lower total from the browser console.
misuseCases.response: The server ignores client totals and refuses the extra field.
tests: a price or total sent by the browser is refused

misuseCases.useCase: A manager refunds a wrong item.
misuseCases.misuseCase: A manager refunds a large bill to an accomplice.
misuseCases.response: Over Rs 5,000 a different person must approve with a fresh code; refund spikes raise an alert.
tests: a large refund waits for a different person with a fresh code

misuseCases.useCase: The kitchen moves an order to Preparing and Ready.
misuseCases.misuseCase: A kitchen user tries to read prices or take a payment.
misuseCases.response: The kitchen receives no prices, and payment routes refuse the role.
tests: the kitchen sees no prices or staff details, and follows the status order
a waiter and the kitchen cannot take payment (finding 7)

misuseCases.useCase: A customer requests a table online.
misuseCases.misuseCase: A bot floods the form, or someone checks whether a number has booked.
misuseCases.response: A limit per address and a hidden field stop bots; the answer is the same either way.
tests: a bot that fills the hidden field is told it worked, but nothing is saved
a repeat gets the same answer, so it cannot reveal who has booked

misuseCases.useCase: A waiter looks up a booking by phone number.
misuseCases.misuseCase: A waiter collects customers' full phone numbers.
misuseCases.response: Waiters see masked numbers; full numbers need a Manager or Admin and are logged.
tests: waiters see a masked phone; only a Manager or Admin can reveal it, with a log entry (finding 32)

misuseCases.useCase: An Admin uploads a photo of a dish.
misuseCases.misuseCase: An attacker uploads an HTML or script file named as a picture.
misuseCases.response: The file signature is checked, and the upload refused and recorded.
tests: scripts, SVG, HTML and disguised files are refused and recorded

misuseCases.useCase: An Admin invites a new waiter.
misuseCases.misuseCase: One Admin secretly creates a second Admin account.
misuseCases.response: Any change affecting an Admin waits for a second Admin.
tests: one Admin alone cannot create another Admin; a second Admin must approve

misuseCases.useCase: An Admin reviews who changed a price.
misuseCases.misuseCase: Someone with database access edits an entry to hide a refund.
misuseCases.response: The chain check finds the change and raises an alert; the app account cannot edit entries.
tests: detects edited details, a changed actor and a changed time

misuseCases.misuseCase: A departing manager exports data again and again.
misuseCases.response: Exports are limited per person, recorded and alerted.
tests: exports are logged, limited per person, and safe to open in a spreadsheet

misuseCases.useCase: The gateway confirms a card payment.
misuseCases.misuseCase: An attacker replays a captured approval callback.
misuseCases.response: Each signed callback is accepted once; a copy is refused and logged.
tests: a copied gateway callback is accepted only once
